problemsData.heading:
Control Room Problems 
 & How We Design Them Out
problemsData.subhead: Most problems in a command control room start at the design stage. We resolve them in the drawings before installation begins.

problem.title: Critical alarms get lost on a busy wall
problem.text: When all feeds get equal space on the wall, operators struggle to find the camera linked to an alarm.

solution.title: Wall layouts that respond to alarms
solution.text: Where platforms allow, saved presets bring the alarm camera and map forward when an alarm is raised.

problem.title: Back-row operators can't read the wall
problem.text: A wall sized only by budget leaves camera tiles and alarm text too small to read from the back row.

solution.title: A wall sized to the farthest console
solution.text: We size the wall and its window layouts from the viewing distance and the smallest content it shows.

problem.title: Too many keyboards on each desk
problem.text: Each system needs its own keyboard and mouse, so operators lose time switching between them.

solution.title: One keyboard for all connected systems
solution.text: KVM over IP lets operators control each system from one keyboard and mouse at their desk.
solution.tag: Clear workspaces with faster control switching

problem.title: A single fault blanks the wall
problem.text: If one controller or power supply fails, the whole wall can go dark in the middle of a shift.

solution.title: Redundancy for continuous operation
solution.text: We specify 24/7 rated panels with backup processing and power, so one fault does not stop the wall.
solution.tag: The wall stays live through a fault

problem.title: Partner agencies lack the same view
problem.text: Outside agencies get updates by phone, so each team builds its own picture of the event.

solution.title: Agencies join through the wall
solution.text: Video conferencing on the wall lets partner agencies see the same map and live feeds as your team.
solution.tag: One shared picture for all teams

problem.title: Any operator can show any feed
problem.text: Without access rules, any operator can send sensitive cameras or data to the shared wall.

solution.title: Role-based access to sources
solution.text: User permissions limit each operator to the sources and wall areas their role allows.

faqHeaderData.heading:
Common Questions on 
 Command & Control Center Solutions

faqData.question: How long does it take to deliver a command and control center?
faqData.answer: Delivery timelines depend primarily on room dimensions and hardware lead times. Standard refits for existing command rooms take less time than constructing a new facility. Our team provides an exact implementation schedule after completing the initial site survey and design review.

faqData.question: Can you upgrade our existing control room without stopping operations?
faqData.answer: Yes, system upgrades can proceed in planned phases to keep primary workstations active during the upgrade work. Installing temporary displays or secondary operator stations preserves continuous monitoring during hardware switchovers. This phased method allows us to deliver command control center upgrades without interrupting daily operational workflows.

faqData.question: Can you build a smart city command and control center?
faqData.answer: Yes. A smart city command and control center brings traffic, utility and public safety feeds together on one shared video wall. Our AV team designs the wall and operator positions while our network team plans secure links to each city platform. City agencies can then work from the same live picture in one control and command centre.

faqData.question: Do you provide monitoring or technical support after handover?
faqData.answer: Yes, for clients under our Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMCs). These AMC packages include routine preventive maintenance visits and rapid technical dispatch, with round-the-clock monitoring available as an optional add-on. Applying these services maintains high reliability across installed control center solutions. Clients without an AMC can request on-demand technical service calls.

faqData.question: Can we connect our existing CCTV and SCADA systems to the new command room?
faqData.answer: Yes, existing security and SCADA software typically integrates through workstation video outputs or local IP video streams. We verify every signal feed during initial planning to deliver a unified integrated command and control center. Our engineers coordinate directly with third-party vendors to establish stable source feeds.

faqData.question: Which standard is used for smart city control room design?
faqData.answer: The ISO 11064 standard serves as the main international reference for control center design, including a smart city integrated command and control centre. This framework guides room layouts, workstation ergonomics, lighting levels, and display sightlines. We apply these standards to support long-term operator focus and comfort.

faqData.question: Can operators or managers view room content from another location?
faqData.answer: Yes, authorized staff can view room content remotely using secure network stream encoding. Establishing an integrated command centre allows administrators to push specific display presets to secondary locations. Encrypted KVM systems also allow designated managers to control local consoles from separate offices.

faqData.question: Will the command center keep working during a power outage?
faqData.answer: Yes, a properly configured command and control room remains functional when backed by an uninterrupted power supply and generator. Our design team calculates exact power draws to assist facility teams with electrical planning. Dual-corded hardware power supplies protect critical display paths during a power supply or feed failure.

faqData.question: Can you work to a consultant design or tender specification?
faqData.answer: Yes, our team deploys custom command and control center solutions based on consultant specifications or formal tender documents. Common command and control center examples include municipal traffic hubs, utility operations, and security centers. If technical discrepancies appear in a tender design, we flag them prior to installation.

faqData.question: How much space does a command center in Dubai typically need?
faqData.answer: Total square footage is driven by video wall scale, console layout, and equipment room requirements. Layouts must incorporate adequate viewing distances and supervisor passage zones for daily operations. Our technical team measures the space during the site survey and confirms precise dimensions at the design stage to build your command center in Dubai.

faqData.question: LCD or LED: which video wall is right for a control room?
faqData.answer: LCD walls are a cost-effective choice for most control rooms and keep the seams between panels very narrow. LED walls have no seams at all, which suits maps and data that span the whole wall. The LED pixel pitch is chosen to match your viewing distance.

faqData.question: Can we see the equipment before it is ordered?
faqData.answer: Yes. Once the design drawings are approved, a product demo lets your team see shortlisted control center solutions in action. Final equipment choices are confirmed only after that session.
